meta.title: BRI Explorer flagship project sample
meta.description: A curated sample of widely reported infrastructure projects associated with the Belt and Road Initiative. It is not a complete inventory. Figures are approximate values as reported in public sources and are not audited; 'BRI' labelling of individual projects varies between sources.

projects.name: Laos–China Railway (Boten–Vientiane)
localPartners: Government of Lao PDR (minority shareholder in the Laos–China Railway Co., Ltd.)
projects.description: A roughly 422 km railway linking the Chinese border at Boten with Vientiane, opened in December 2021 and connected to the Kunming line in China. It is operated by the Laos–China Railway Company, a joint venture majority-owned by Chinese state companies.

projects.name: Jakarta–Bandung High-Speed Railway (Whoosh)
projects.location: Halim (Jakarta) to Tegalluar (Bandung), West Java, Indonesia
chineseEntities: China Railway International consortium (Beijing Yawan HSR Co.)
localPartners: PT Kereta Cepat Indonesia China (KCIC) joint venture
PSBI consortium of Indonesian state-owned enterprises incl. PT Kereta Api Indonesia and Wijaya Karya
projects.description: A 142 km high-speed line between Jakarta and Bandung, Southeast Asia's first high-speed railway, which began commercial service in October 2023. Construction costs rose above the original estimate, and the overrun was financed with additional loans.

projects.name: Mombasa–Nairobi Standard Gauge Railway
projects.location: Mombasa to Nairobi (Phase 2A extension to Naivasha), Kenya

cost.display: ≈ US$3.2 billion for Phase 1 (reported); Phase 2A to Naivasha financed separately

projects.description: A roughly 470 km standard gauge railway between the port of Mombasa and Nairobi that opened in 2017; a Phase 2A extension towards Naivasha opened in 2019. It was largely financed by loans from the Export-Import Bank of China.

projects.name: Addis Ababa–Djibouti Railway
projects.location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia to Port of Djibouti

cost.display: ≈ US$4 billion (reported), largely financed by the Export-Import Bank of China

projects.description: A roughly 750 km electrified railway connecting landlocked Ethiopia with the port of Djibouti. It was inaugurated in 2016 and began commercial operations in 2018. Construction began before the BRI was announced, and the line is now commonly cited as a BRI project.

projects.name: Budapest–Belgrade Railway modernisation
projects.statusNote: The Serbian section runs passenger services to Subotica. Hungarian section works are reported complete and freight began in February 2026; the start of passenger service was still pending as of mid-2026.

cost.display: Hungarian section reportedly ≈ US$2 billion, about 85% loan-financed by the Export-Import Bank of China; Serbian sections financed separately

chineseEntities: China Railway Group (CREC) / China Railway International
localPartners: Government of Serbia / Infrastruktura železnice Srbije
projects.description: A roughly 350 km upgrade of the railway between Budapest and Belgrade. It is often described as part of the 'China–Europe Land-Sea Express' linking the Port of Piraeus with Central Europe.

projects.name: Lagos–Ibadan Standard Gauge Railway
projects.description: A roughly 156 km standard gauge line between Lagos and Ibadan that began commercial service in 2021, as part of Nigeria's wider Lagos–Kano modernisation plan.

projects.name: East Coast Rail Link (ECRL)
projects.location: Kota Bharu (Kelantan) to Port Klang (Selangor), Peninsular Malaysia
projects.statusNote: Malaysian government statements targeted the start of operations around the end of 2026 / early 2027.

cost.display: RM50.27 billion (revised estimate announced in 2023; roughly US$11 billion)

localPartners: Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL, project owner)
projects.description: A rail line of about 665 km linking Malaysia's east coast states with Port Klang on the west coast. The project was renegotiated and re-scoped in 2019 and its alignment and cost were revised.

projects.name: Bangkok–Nakhon Ratchasima High-Speed Railway (Phase 1)
projects.location: Bangkok (Bang Sue) to Nakhon Ratchasima, Thailand

cost.display: ≈ 179 billion baht (Thai government budget, reported); no single USD figure used

chineseEntities: China Railway International (systems, rolling stock & training contract)
projects.description: The first 253 km phase of a planned high-speed line intended to connect Bangkok with the Laos–China Railway at Nong Khai. Thailand is financing the civil works itself, and Chinese firms provide design, systems and rolling stock.

projects.name: China–Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan Railway
projects.location: Kashgar (China) via Torugart and Jalal-Abad (Kyrgyzstan) to Andijan (Uzbekistan)
projects.statusNote: Construction was formally launched in December 2024. The alignment shown is approximate.
chineseEntities: China State Railway Group (through a trilateral joint venture, reported)
projects.description: A cross-border railway that was discussed for more than two decades and is intended to give China a southern rail route to Central Asia and beyond without passing through Kazakhstan or Russia.

projects.name: Hanoi Metro Line 2A (Cát Linh–Hà Đông)
projects.description: Vietnam's first metro line, about 13 km of elevated track, which opened in November 2021 after years of delays and cost increases. Construction began before the BRI was announced.

projects.name: Lahore Metro Orange Line
chineseEntities: China Railway Group & China North Industries Corp. (NORINCO) consortium
projects.description: A roughly 27 km automated metro line, Pakistan's first, which opened in October 2020 and is listed among CPEC projects.

projects.name: Padma Bridge Rail Link
projects.location: Dhaka via the Padma Bridge to Jessore, Bangladesh
projects.statusNote: The Dhaka–Bhanga section opened in 2023 and the Bhanga–Jessore section in 2024.

cost.display: Total reported at about Tk 39,000 crore; Chinese concessional loan reported at ≈ US$2.67 billion

projects.description: A railway of about 170 km that uses the rail deck of the Padma Bridge to link Dhaka with southwestern Bangladesh. The bridge itself was financed by Bangladesh and built by a Chinese contractor.

projects.name: Gwadar Port
projects.statusNote: The port operates with comparatively limited commercial traffic, according to public reporting.
chineseEntities: China Overseas Port Holding Company (operator since 2013)
projects.description: A deep-sea port on the Arabian Sea, originally built in the 2000s with Chinese assistance. Operations were transferred to China Overseas Port Holding Company in 2013. It is the southern anchor of the China–Pakistan Economic Corridor.

projects.name: Hambantota International Port

cost.display: US$1.12 billion paid by China Merchants Port Holdings in 2017 for a 70% stake and a 99-year concession (reported)

projects.description: A port built in phases from 2008 with Chinese loans. In 2017 a 70% stake was leased to China Merchants Port Holdings for 99 years, a transaction that is widely discussed and interpreted differently by different analysts.

projects.name: Port City Colombo
projects.statusNote: Land reclamation was completed in 2019; development of the built-up area is ongoing.

cost.display: ≈ US$1.4 billion direct investment by CHEC for reclamation and infrastructure (reported)

chineseEntities: China Harbour Engineering Company (CHEC Port City Colombo)
projects.description: A district of about 269 hectares built on land reclaimed next to Colombo's central business district and planned as a special economic zone with its own regulatory commission.

projects.name: Port of Piraeus (COSCO stake)

cost.display: €280.5 million for a 51% stake in the Piraeus Port Authority (2016); stake later raised to 67% (reported)

projects.description: COSCO has operated container piers at Piraeus since a 2009 concession and became majority owner of the port authority in 2016. Piraeus is often described as the Maritime Silk Road's main gateway into Europe.

projects.name: Doraleh Multipurpose Port
chineseEntities: China Merchants Port Holdings (minority shareholder in Port de Djibouti S.A.)
projects.description: A multipurpose port that opened in 2017 at the southern entrance of the Red Sea and is linked to the Addis Ababa–Djibouti Railway.

projects.name: Port of Chancay

cost.display: ≈ US$1.3 billion for the first phase (reported); total planned investment reported up to ≈ US$3.5 billion

projects.description: A deep-water port about 70 km north of Lima, inaugurated in November 2024 and designed to handle large container ships on direct Asia–South America routes.

projects.name: Kyaukphyu Deep Sea Port
projects.statusNote: Agreements were signed in 2018–2020, but progress has been limited and affected by Myanmar's political situation and conflict.

cost.display: First phase scaled down to ≈ US$1.3 billion in 2018 (reported, from an earlier ≈ US$7.3 billion plan); not counted in totals because it is unbuilt

projects.description: A planned deep-sea port on the Bay of Bengal at the start of the existing Myanmar–China oil and gas pipelines. It is a central element of the China–Myanmar Economic Corridor.

projects.name: Lekki Deep Sea Port
projects.description: A deep-sea port east of Lagos that began commercial operations in 2023. It is intended to ease congestion at the older Apapa and Tin Can Island ports.

projects.name: Khorgos Gateway Dry Port
chineseEntities: COSCO Shipping and Lianyungang Port (combined minority stake from 2017, reported)
projects.description: An inland port on the Kazakhstan–China border where containers are transferred between Chinese standard-gauge and Kazakh broad-gauge trains on China–Europe rail routes.

projects.name: Karakoram Highway Phase II (Havelian–Thakot)
projects.location: Havelian to Thakot, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan

cost.display: ≈ US$1.3 billion (reported), financed by the Export-Import Bank of China

projects.description: A roughly 118 km upgrade of the Karakoram Highway corridor north of Islamabad, completed in 2020 as a CPEC transport project.

projects.name: Multan–Sukkur Motorway (M-5)
projects.description: A roughly 392 km six-lane motorway that opened in 2019 as part of the Peshawar–Karachi motorway under CPEC.

projects.name: Bar–Boljare Motorway (Smokovac–Mateševo section)
projects.statusNote: The priority section opened in 2022; the rest of the planned motorway has not been built.

cost.display: ≈ US$944 million loan from the Export-Import Bank of China covering about 85% of the priority section (reported)

projects.description: A 41 km mountainous priority section of a planned motorway from the Adriatic port of Bar to the Serbian border. Its cost relative to Montenegro's economy has been the subject of public debate.

projects.name: Nairobi Expressway
projects.location: Mlolongo / JKIA to Westlands, Nairobi, Kenya

cost.display: ≈ US$600–670 million (reported range), privately financed under a public-private partnership

chineseEntities: China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC, concessionaire via Moja Expressway)
projects.description: A 27 km toll road through Nairobi, built and financed by CRBC under a build-operate-transfer arrangement and opened to traffic in 2022.

projects.name: Phnom Penh–Sihanoukville Expressway
chineseEntities: China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC, build-operate-transfer)
localPartners: Ministry of Public Works and Transport (Cambodia)
projects.description: Cambodia's first expressway, about 187 km long, linking the capital with its main deep-water port. It opened in 2022.

projects.name: Pelješac Bridge
projects.location: Komarna to the Pelješac peninsula, Dubrovnik-Neretva County, Croatia

cost.display: ≈ €420 million including access roads, about 85% co-financed by EU cohesion funds (reported); not Chinese-financed

chineseEntities: China Road and Bridge Corporation (lead contractor, consortium)
projects.description: A 2.4 km bridge connecting southern Dalmatia with the rest of Croatia. It is included as an example of a Chinese contractor winning an EU-funded tender, and it is not BRI-financed, which shows how 'BRI project' labels can differ between sources.

projects.name: Sinamalé Bridge (China–Maldives Friendship Bridge)

cost.display: ≈ US$200 million, financed by a Chinese grant and loan (reported)

projects.description: A 2.1 km sea bridge connecting the capital Malé with the airport island. It opened in 2018.

projects.name: Kampala–Entebbe Expressway

cost.display: ≈ US$476 million (reported), largely financed by the Export-Import Bank of China

projects.description: A 51 km four-lane toll expressway between the capital and Uganda's international airport that opened in 2018. Construction began before the BRI was announced.

projects.name: Sahiwal Coal Power Plant
projects.description: A 1,320 MW coal-fired plant that was among the first CPEC energy projects to start commercial operation, in 2017.

projects.name: Port Qasim Coal Power Plant
projects.description: A 1,320 MW imported-coal power plant near Karachi that began commercial operation in 2018 as a CPEC priority energy project.

references.label: Wikipedia: Port Qasim Coal Power Plant

projects.name: Karot Hydropower Project
projects.location: Jhelum River, Punjab / Azad Jammu and Kashmir border, Pakistan
chineseEntities: China Three Gorges Corporation (via CTG South Asia Investment Ltd.)
Export-Import Bank of China & China Development Bank (lenders)
projects.description: A 720 MW run-of-river hydropower plant that reached commercial operation in 2022. It was the Silk Road Fund's first investment. The International Finance Corporation was also among the financiers.

projects.name: Matiari–Lahore ±660 kV HVDC Transmission Line
chineseEntities: State Grid Corporation of China (via Pak Matiari-Lahore Transmission Company)
projects.description: An approximately 880 km high-voltage direct-current line carrying power from southern generation sites to load centres in Punjab. It was Pakistan's first HVDC line and entered commercial operation in 2021. The route shown is approximate.

projects.name: Coca Codo Sinclair Hydroelectric Plant
projects.location: Coca River, Napo / Sucumbíos provinces, Ecuador
projects.statusNote: Public reporting has documented technical problems, including cracks in plant components and river erosion upstream.

cost.display: ≈ US$2.2 billion contract value (reported), about 85% financed by the Export-Import Bank of China

projects.description: Ecuador's largest hydropower plant, completed in 2016. Construction began before the BRI was announced and before Ecuador's 2018 BRI memorandum. It is frequently discussed in analyses of Chinese lending in Latin America.

references.label: Wikipedia: Coca Codo Sinclair Hydroelectric Project

projects.name: Lower Sesan II Hydropower Dam
projects.location: Sesan River, Stung Treng Province, Cambodia
projects.description: A 400 MW dam near the Mekong confluence that was completed in 2018. Its effects on fisheries and on resettled communities have been documented by researchers and NGOs.

projects.name: Payra Thermal Power Plant
chineseEntities: China National Machinery Import & Export Corporation (CMC, 50% JV partner)
localPartners: North-West Power Generation Company Ltd. (NWPGCL, 50% JV partner)
projects.description: A 1,320 MW coal-fired plant developed by a 50:50 Bangladeshi–Chinese joint venture. It reached full commercial operation in 2020.

projects.name: Hunutlu Thermal Power Plant
chineseEntities: State Power Investment Corporation (SPIC, majority shareholder)
projects.description: A 1,320 MW imported-coal power plant on the Mediterranean coast. It is often reported as one of the largest Chinese direct investments in Türkiye.

projects.name: Noor Energy 1 (Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park, Phase IV)
projects.location: Saih Al-Dahal, Dubai, United Arab Emirates
projects.description: A 950 MW project combining concentrated solar power, including a solar tower, with photovoltaic panels. It was fully completed in 2023.

references.label: Wikipedia: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park

projects.name: Myanmar–China Oil and Gas Pipelines
projects.location: Kyaukphyu (Rakhine State, Myanmar) to Kunming (Yunnan, China)
projects.statusNote: The gas pipeline began operating in 2013 and the oil pipeline in 2017. The route shown is approximate.

cost.display: ≈ US$2.5 billion for the Myanmar sections (reported)

projects.description: Parallel crude-oil and natural-gas pipelines that let some of China's energy imports bypass the Strait of Malacca. They were planned before the BRI and are now considered part of the China–Myanmar Economic Corridor.

projects.name: Caculo Cabaça Hydroelectric Project
chineseEntities: China Energy Engineering Group – Gezhouba (CGGC, contractor)
Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (lender, reported)
projects.description: A planned 2,172 MW hydropower plant on the Kwanza River. On completion it would be among the largest in Africa.

references.label: Wikipedia: Caculo Cabaça Hydroelectric Power Station

projects.name: Cauchari Solar Park

cost.display: ≈ US$390 million (reported), mostly financed by the Export-Import Bank of China

localPartners: JEMSE (Jujuy Energía y Minería Sociedad del Estado)
projects.description: A 300 MW solar park at about 4,000 m altitude in the Andes, among the highest-elevation large PV plants. It began operating in 2020, before Argentina joined the BRI in 2022.

projects.name: China–Belarus Industrial Park "Great Stone"
projects.description: A special economic zone near Minsk National Airport that hosts Chinese, Belarusian and other foreign companies. It was established under a 2011 intergovernmental agreement.

projects.name: New Administrative Capital Central Business District
projects.location: New Administrative Capital, east of Cairo, Egypt
projects.statusNote: Major towers, including the Iconic Tower, were completed in the early 2020s. Wider development of the city is ongoing.

cost.display: ≈ US$3 billion (reported), largely financed by a consortium of Chinese banks

projects.description: A district of about 20 high-rise towers in Egypt's new capital, including the Iconic Tower, which is reported as Africa's tallest building.

projects.name: Indonesia Morowali Industrial Park (IMIP)
projects.description: A large industrial park for nickel smelting and stainless-steel production, established in 2013. It is central to Indonesia's downstream nickel policy, and labour and environmental conditions there have been reported on widely.

projects.name: New Gwadar International Airport

cost.display: ≈ US$246 million, financed by a Chinese government grant (reported)

projects.description: A new international airport serving Gwadar, built as a CPEC project and inaugurated in late 2024. Commercial flights began in January 2025.
